key_insight: Teach a model what to draw before teaching it how to render. The paper separates visual generation into autoregressive pretraining for semantic knowledge and diffusion post-training for fine-grained visual detail.
problem_solved: Visual generation must combine high-level understanding with pixel-level fidelity, but these abilities may benefit from different training objectives.
method: Use autoregressive pretraining to acquire high-level semantic knowledge.
Apply diffusion post-training to learn high-fidelity rendering.
Study training objectives, representations, and scaling; controlled comparisons favor autoregression for pretraining before downstream rendering.
impact: This approach suggests a practical way to divide training between semantic learning and visual rendering. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific performance gains and efficiency benefits cannot be established.
visual_elements: Two-stage pipeline: autoregressive pretraining → diffusion post-training → generated image.
Paired icons: a brain for semantic knowledge and a paintbrush for fine-grained rendering.
Concept-to-detail illustration showing scene relationships followed by textures and lighting.
Qualitative comparison panel highlighting the reported advantage of autoregressive pretraining, without inventing numerical results.
paper_title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
paper_authors: Yucheng Mao, Chongjian Ge, Zhuowen Tu, Hao Tan, Hanwen Jiang
